title: Visit-Fee Credit on Stalled Repairs — Homeowner Service Contracts Cash Settlements
content:
For a customer-elected settlement on a request whose repair authorization stalled and was reversed, and only for such a settlement, the standard visit fee collected on that request is credited in the cash at the stall fee share described below, while fees are still not refunded because a failure is determined not covered or because the customer declines a covered repair or replacement; every other fee remains under the general service call fee rule. This applies to Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts.

**Credit.** The stall fee credit is the standard visit fee collected on the request multiplied by the stall fee share and rounded to the cent. It is added to the cash starting figure before that figure is compared with the remaining item and aggregate benefits.

**Stall span.** The stall span is the calendar days from the date of the request's repair authorization to the date of that authorization's reversal.

**Stall fee share.** The tier's parts lead time is 14 days on every tier of Homeowner Service Contracts.

| Stall span | Share |
|---|---|
| at least 4 times the parts lead time (56 days or more) | 1.00, the full fee |
| at least 2 times but less than 4 times the parts lead time (28 to 55 days) | 0.50, half the fee |
| shorter than 2 times the parts lead time (27 days or fewer), or the request carries no reversed repair authorization | nothing |

**Edge values.** A span of 56 days takes the full fee; 55 days takes half; 28 days takes half; 27 days takes nothing.

**Example (hypothetical).** Repair authorized March 1, reversed April 10: the span is 40 days, so the share is 0.50. With a 125.00 standard visit fee collected on the request, the stall fee credit is 62.50.
